summary: Researched on the evening of Wed 11 Nov for Thursday. 16 candidates (14 more were added later with --more and not researched) (Nations League football, EuroLeague, ice hockey, ATP Stockholm, WTA Finals, CS2); 8 researched, 8 not reached because six games were already kept at medium confidence. Medium confidence: England over Croatia (Croatia effectively out of the group, England won the first meeting 7-0, but Konsa, Guehi, Saka, Palmer and others are out and Spain away follows on Sunday; p 0.77), Czechia v Spain (Spain already qualified and without Yamal, Oyarzabal, Rodri and Olmo, England next; p 0.80), Montenegro over Latvia (group leaders at home against a side with little to play for; p 0.765), Michelsen over Tabilo (fresher, better hard-court Elo, won their only meeting; p 0.74), Spirit over G2 (CS2 BLAST Rivals Bo3 on LAN, Spirit top 2 and 2-0 in the last meeting; p 0.73) and Gauff over Kostyuk (Kostyuk eliminated with a wrist problem; Gauff's own motivation is thin; p 0.68). Low confidence, never bet: Real Madrid v Crvena Zvezda (Campazzo, Maledon, Jantunen out; no lineups or rating). Excluded: Hurricanes v Kraken (NHL Global Series in Helsinki, neutral venue). Team news may change on match day, so the slip is rebuilt if the research is pushed again before its first game. No Stake or Rainbet prices were found; prices seen were DraftKings via ESPN for the football, Codere for Real Madrid, and tips.gg / footballpredictions listings for Montenegro. Pre-kickoff check at 19:10 Belgrade: Montenegro v Latvia, England v Croatia, Czechia v Spain and Kostyuk v Gauff re-checked with live prices. All four stay medium: official lineups were not out yet. Montenegro shortened (DraftKings 1.36 to 1.24) and can seal promotion with a win; Loncar suspended. England confirmed Kane starts, the back line is reshuffled (Konsa, Guehi, Spence out) and the price eased slightly; Croatia near full strength apart from Perisic. Spain: Laporte a late illness doubt and the price drifted slightly; no heavy rotation confirmed. Gauff: order of play confirmed (first on), Kostyuk still listed with a wrist problem; the market rose to 0.755 with no news found, above the Elo ratings.

checks.team_news: Morning findings still hold: Yamal (right knee, stayed in Barcelona) and Oyarzabal (did not travel) miss Prague; Rodri and Dani Olmo out; Barrenetxea replaced by De Frutos. NEW today (Sportaragon/OKDiario previews, 12 Nov): Laporte is a late doubt with a viral/flu-like illness, probably out. No new Czechia injury news found; Denia had not announced his XI or medical updates when the previews were published. ESPN summary for event 401861148 is still Scheduled with no rosters.
checks.lineups: No confirmed XI yet (ESPN rosters empty, status Scheduled), so nothing is confirmed. Predicted today: Spain (OKDiario) Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Huijsen, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Fabian, Merino; Fermin, Baena, Ferran Torres. Sportaragon variant: Simon; Porro, Laporte, Cubarsi, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Fabian, Baena, Fermin; Ferran, Pino, with Huijsen or Merino as alternatives. Starting goalkeeper expected to be Unai Simon, unconfirmed. Czechia (Sportaragon, unconfirmed): Kovar; Coufal, Zima, Krejci, Chaloupek, Jurasek; Sadilek, Soucek, Kral, Provod; Hlozek. Key question, how many changes De la Fuente makes: no confirmed count and no press-conference quote found. OKDiario names only one change (Merino in for Nico Williams) and gives no total. Even this predicted XI is a reshuffled side without Yamal, Oyarzabal, Rodri and Olmo, but it keeps Simon, Cubarsi, Cucurella, Zubimendi, Fabian and Ferran, so it is not an obvious wholesale rotation.
checks.rotation: Unchanged from the morning: Spain are already qualified and play England on Sunday 15 Nov at the Metropolitano. Yamal and Oyarzabal are being held back for that game. In October De la Fuente made 9 changes against Croatia and still won 3-1 in Oviedo, so heavy rotation is possible again. Today's predicted XIs suggest a strong but reshuffled side, not a confirmed heavy rotation.
checks.motivation: Unchanged: Spain 12 pts and through, England 9, Croatia 3, Czechia 0. Czechia are at home, bottom of the group, and fighting to avoid League B relegation, so they are highly motivated. Spain have lower stakes.
checks.form: Unchanged: Spain won all 4 Nations League games (3-2 v England, 2-1 v Croatia, 3-1 v Czechia, plus one more). Czechia lost all 4, but scored against Spain in October.
checks.h2h: Unchanged: 3 Oct 2026 Spain 3-1 Czechia in Oviedo, with Spain rotating 9 players. 2022-23 Nations League: Czechia 2-2 Spain in Prague and Spain 2-0 in Malaga.
checks.odds: Refreshed 18:07 UTC. Polymarket live: Spain 0.8036, draw 0.1328, Czechia 0.0636. Morning was 0.8164 / 0.1171 / 0.0665, so Spain is down about 1.3 points and the draw is up about 1.6 points. Polymarket move_24h shows Spain 0.815 to 0.805, a small drift against the favourite. DraftKings decimal: Spain 1.22 (opened 1.15), draw 6.0 (opened 7.0), Czechia 10.5 (opened 12). De-vigged: Spain 0.758, draw 0.154, Czechia 0.088. The book has lengthened Spain since opening and the book is lower than Polymarket on Spain. DK total 3.5.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net) now available: Spain 2287 vs Czechia 1656, a gap of 631, expected score for Czechia 0.045. That supports Spain as a clear favourite, but the rating does not capture the missing Yamal, Oyarzabal, Rodri and Olmo or the low stakes. Elo agrees on direction; the bookmaker is lower on Spain than Polymarket, so sources do not fully agree on the exact level.
checks.venue_weather: Generali Arena (Letna), Prague, Czechia's home ground, 20:45 local (19:45 UTC). A normal home venue, not neutral. No weather or pitch problem found.

games.reason: Re-checked 90 minutes before kick-off. Nothing confirmed: no official XI, Laporte is a new late doubt (illness), and Spain's price has drifted slightly down (0.816 to 0.804) while the draw rose (0.117 to 0.133), with DraftKings also lengthening Spain from the 1.15 open. Predicted XIs show a reshuffled but still strong Spain side, not a confirmed heavy rotation, so no exclusion. Spain win 0.79 against live 0.8036, draw 0.14. Confidence stays medium because the lineup and goalkeeper are unconfirmed, Laporte is doubtful, and the price moved slightly against the leg.
games.main_risk: Spain, already qualified and with England on Sunday, rotate heavily or are flat without four key players, and a motivated Czechia at home, fighting relegation, draw or upset. The draw is the main way the leg fails: the market draw rose to 0.133 and the DraftKings de-vigged draw is 0.154. Laporte's illness and an unconfirmed XI add late uncertainty.

checks.team_news: Morning findings hold: Konsa and Spence out (Tuchel presser, 11 Nov), Guehi withdrawn (Burn called up as replacement per Yahoo), Saka, Palmer, Rashford, Mainoo and others missing. New today: Kane is confirmed by the manager to start (record 126th cap). Croatia: Perisic suspended (Sports Mole); Sutalo, Pongracic, Jakic, Kramaric and others out. Modric, Kovacic, Gvardiol and Vuskovic appear in every predicted Croatia XI and no injury is reported for Modric or Gvardiol, so Croatia look close to full strength in midfield and defence, minus Perisic. No new injury or illness news found today.
checks.lineups: Not confirmed. ESPN summary (event 401861150) has no roster or formation yet. Today's web search found only predicted XIs, and they disagree on England's defence: Sports Mole has Alexander-Arnold, Quansah, Branthwaite, Hall (Konsa out); Yahoo uses Burn; Tribal Football lists Konsa, which is outdated. Pickford is the expected England keeper. Croatia predicted: Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Caleta-Car, Gvardiol; Modric, Kovacic; Vlasic, Pasalic, Baturina; Budimir (Tribal's Perisic start is outdated). England's attack looks decent with Kane, Bellingham and Gordon, but thinner than usual without Saka, Palmer and Rashford. No official XI yet.
checks.rotation: England have Spain away on Sunday 15 Nov, so some rotation or minutes management is possible, but nothing is confirmed and the squad is already thin. No 5+ changes announced, so no hard exclusion. Croatia face Czechia on Sunday and are not expected to rotate, since they need a result.
checks.motivation: Unchanged from the morning. England (9 pts) are close to sealing a quarter-final place. Croatia (3 pts) are effectively out and need a big win. Spain on Sunday decides the group, which may lead Tuchel to manage minutes.
checks.form: Unchanged: England DWWLW, with a 7-0 win in Rijeka in October. Croatia DLLWL, having lost 7 of their last 11.
checks.h2h: Unchanged: England have 8 wins, 2 draws and 3 defeats in 13 meetings, and won 7-0 most recently in Rijeka.
checks.odds: DraftKings (ESPN, fetched 18:07 UTC): England 1.24 (opening 1.24), draw 6.0 (opening 5.5), Croatia 10.0 (opening 9.5), total 3.5. De-vigged 0.752 / 0.155 / 0.093. Polymarket live 0.7735 / 0.1529 / 0.0736. England's price has eased 2 points in 24h (0.795 to 0.775) and the draw has drifted slightly longer, a mild move against the leg that is consistent with the Konsa/Guehi defensive news and with expected rotation. No price shock. Live legs: +2.5 Croatia at 0.655, England -1.5 at 0.565, over 2.5 at 0.665, under 3.5 at 0.565, under 4.5 at 0.745.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): England 2146, Croatia 1856, a 290-point gap and expected score for England of 0.904. That agrees with the market on England being strong favourites, since expected score includes half the draw. Odds and rating sources agree.
checks.venue_weather: Wembley Stadium, London (ESPN confirms), kick-off 19:45 UTC. No weather or pitch alert found, and no forecast was checked.

games.reason: England remain clear favourites at Wembley. Croatia are close to full strength in midfield and defence (Modric, Kovacic, Gvardiol), missing only Perisic, but they are weak overall (Elo 1856 vs 2146, beaten 7-0 in the first meeting). England have no confirmed XI, a reshuffled back line (Konsa, Guehi, Spence out) and rotation risk with Spain on Sunday, though Kane starts. For Croatia +2.5, the leg loses only if England win by 3 or more. The 7-0 first meeting shows that tail is real, but England's attack is thinner (no Saka, Palmer, Rashford) and the market puts the 3+ margin near 35%. I put the +2.5 leg at 0.66, in line with the market. Confidence stays medium because the lineup is unconfirmed and England's price eased slightly, so I am not marking it high.
games.main_risk: A heavy England win. They scored 7 in the first meeting, and the 3+ goal margin, which is what beats Croatia +2.5, is still about a one-in-three chance. Secondary risks are an unconfirmed XI and England managing minutes before Spain.

checks.team_news: Morning findings still hold. New today: Sports Mole's Gameweek 5 preview (found in a search today) confirms Montenegro midfielder Stefan Loncar is suspended after a red card in the Armenia game. It also says Latvia are without Kristers Penkevics, who last played in a June friendly. Starting11 lists Andrej Duric as unavailable, which conflicts with Sports Mole's predicted back line, so his status is unclear. No other late injury or illness news found. Latvia's wider squad status (Ikaunieks, Uldrikis, Tobers and others) is still unknown.
checks.lineups: Not confirmed. The ESPN summary for this match (event 401861152) had empty rosters when checked, about 90 minutes before kick-off. Predicted: Montenegro with Popovic in goal, Jovetic and Krstovic up front and a changed midfield because of Loncar's suspension. Latvia in a 5-4-1 with Matrevics in goal and Gutkovskis up front (Sports Mole, Starting11). Official XIs are due about an hour before kick-off.
checks.rotation: No heavy-rotation report for Montenegro. Sports Mole says a win would seal top spot and automatic promotion with a game to spare, so Montenegro have a strong reason to field a full side. Latvia travel for an away game before hosting Armenia on 15 Nov.
checks.motivation: Montenegro lead League C Group 2 and can secure promotion with a win tonight. Latvia are fourth with 1 point and have little to play for. This is unchanged from the morning, and the promotion detail is new today.
checks.form: Unchanged from the morning. Montenegro beat Cyprus 2-1 and Armenia 3-2 and won 2-1 at Latvia. They have conceded in each of those wins. Latvia lost 0-2 at Armenia and 1-2 at home to Montenegro.
checks.h2h: Reverse fixture on 2 Oct 2026: Latvia 1-2 Montenegro in Riga. Both teams scored in that game, which supports lower confidence on BTTS no.
checks.odds: Polymarket live de-vig is 0.7765 / 0.157 / 0.066, against 0.7565 / 0.167 / 0.076 in the morning. DraftKings via ESPN now has Montenegro 1.24, draw 5.50, Latvia 11.00, de-vigged 0.748 / 0.168 / 0.084. It opened at 1.36 / 4.50 / 7.50. The 24h move on the Montenegro win token is 0.755 to 0.775, which is in the leg's favour and not a concern. Live Polymarket and DraftKings agree to within about 3 points.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net, refreshed today): Montenegro 1489, Latvia 1246, expected home score 0.878. This supports Montenegro as clear favourites. Elo expected score counts a draw as half a win, so it is not directly comparable with the win probability. Footballpredictions.com, Footballpredictions.ai and Kickoff.co.uk all had Montenegro as favourites in the morning, with a 2-1 modal score.
checks.venue_weather: Podgorica City Stadium (ESPN), home ground, kick-off 19:45 UTC. No weather or pitch problem found, and I did not find a forecast, so conditions are unverified.

games.reason: Montenegro are group leaders at home against a fourth-placed Latvia side with little to play for, and a win secures promotion. The live market (0.7765) and DraftKings de-vig (0.748) agree, and Elo points the same way, so p stays near the market. Confidence stays medium because lineups are not confirmed, Loncar is suspended and Duric's status is unclear. A draw is estimated at 16%, under the 25% limit for a straight win.
games.main_risk: A draw or narrow result against a deep-defending 5-4-1 Latvia. Loncar is suspended, XIs are unconfirmed, and Montenegro have conceded in every recent game. Latvia's squad news is unknown.

checks.team_news: No injury or withdrawal reports found for either player in searches on 11 Nov. Both are in the draw and both won on the ATP Stockholm results page. Michelsen beat Hanfmann 6-2 6-3 (R1) and J.M. Cerundolo 6-3 6-2 (R16, Tue 10 Nov, completed per ATP and Mykhel). Tabilo (4th seed, R1 bye) beat qualifier Sonego 7-6(2) 6-7(7) 7-5 on Wed 11 Nov on Center Court. Nothing announced about injury, but he played a long three-set match, so fatigue is a risk. Not confirmed: any physical issue for either player.
checks.lineups: Order of play for Thu 12 Nov not published on the ATP pages I could read (daily schedule only showed Day 5). Not confirmed: court and time. The candidate file has the start at 12:00 UTC. The round is most likely the quarter-final: Michelsen and Tabilo have both won their R16 matches. I did not see the official bracket.
checks.rotation: Michelsen: straight sets twice, about 1h08 in R1 and a short R16, so he is fresh. Tabilo: 3 sets with two tiebreaks (7-6, 6-7, 7-5) on Wed, then back on Thu with one day of rest, a clear fatigue edge to Michelsen. Same venue, no travel for either.
checks.motivation: ATP 250 quarter-final, a place in the semi-final, ranking points and prize money at the end of the season. Both are playing in the last tournament of the ATP week (8-14 Nov). No sign of either having less to play for.
checks.form: Michelsen: won both Stockholm matches in straight sets, 4 sets lost 5 games in R1 and 5 games in R16 (6-2 6-3, 6-3 6-2). Tabilo: needed three sets and 2 tiebreaks to get past Sonego (qualifier). Results from before Stockholm were not checked.
checks.h2h: One meeting: Miami Open R3, hard court, 23 Mar 2026, Michelsen won in three sets (stringtension shows the score as 3-6 6-3 6-4 in compressed form; reading inferred). Michelsen leads 1-0. Tabilo is a left-hander.
checks.odds: No bookmaker price found besides Polymarket. Searches returned only March 2026 Miami odds (Stats Insider Michelsen about 58%, Tabilo $2.37, Michelsen $1.57). I did not get a de-vigged price for the Stockholm match, nor the 24h Polymarket move. Market p is Michelsen 0.75, Tabilo 0.25 per candidates file. This is a gap in the checks.
checks.models: Tennis Abstract Elo (list updated 2026-11-09): Michelsen Elo 1879.9 (rank 25), hard Elo 1851.6 (rank 19). Tabilo Elo 1782.2 (rank 59), hard Elo 1731.8 (rank 57). The hard-Elo gap of 120 points implies about 67% for Michelsen, below the 75% market. The fatigue edge and the h2h partly support the market.
checks.venue_weather: Kungliga Tennishallen, Stockholm: indoor hard court, no weather impact, same venue for both players all week.

games.reason: Fixture verified: Bybit Stockholm Open (ATP 250), Michelsen (6th seed) v Tabilo (4th seed), both through R16 on 10 and 11 Nov. Michelsen is the better player on hard-court Elo (about 120 hElo points), is fresher after two straight-set wins, and leads the h2h 1-0. Tabilo played 3 sets with 2 tiebreaks the day before. Elo implies about 67%, below the market 75%, so p is set at 0.74, one point under the market. Confidence medium, not high, because the order of play is unconfirmed and no second price source was found.
games.main_risk: Tabilo is a left-hander with a big serve and a tight match is decided in a few points; indoor 250 matches can turn on a tiebreak. Elo says Michelsen should be nearer 67% than 75%. Missing facts: Thursday order of play and a non-Polymarket price.

checks.team_news: No injuries, illness or stand-ins reported for either side in any source read today. tips.gg preview (9 Nov) lists Spirit as magixx, zont1x, donk, sh1ro, tN1R (coach hally) and G2 as huNter-, HeavyGod, matys, NertZ, r1nkle (coach sAw), with no stand-ins listed. Strafe notes only that FUT signed SunPayus. HLTV and the team socials were not reachable, so this rests on preview articles.
checks.lineups: Predicted fives only, from one preview source (tips.gg), with nothing official found: Spirit magixx/zont1x/donk/sh1ro/tN1R; G2 huNter-/HeavyGod/matys/NertZ/r1nkle. Both teams played their groups' opening matches on 11 Nov with these names per the listing, and no change was reported.
checks.rotation: Group B opening matches were Spirit 2-1 FUT (11 Nov, ~06:30) and G2 2-1 MOUZ (11 Nov, ~09:36) per esportnow.gg, both Bo3. The 12 Nov Spirit-G2 Bo3 at 09:30 is the winners' match of a double-elimination group (both teams 1-0), so the loser still gets an elimination game. Spirit played a full three-map match yesterday, so there is some fatigue risk, but G2 also went three maps and both sit on the same LAN schedule. Spirit won BLAST Open Porto in late Aug 2026.
checks.motivation: Winners' match of the four-team double-elimination Group B. The top 3 of 4 advance, and the group winner goes straight to the semifinals while #2 and #3 start in the quarterfinals. Both teams are already close to qualifying, so the stake is the semifinal bye, and neither side is under elimination pressure.
checks.form: Spirit: won BLAST Open Porto (Aug 2026, beat MOUZ 3-1 in the final), HLTV top 2 in late October per tips.gg, and beat FUT 2-1 on 11 Nov (dropped a map). G2: beat MOUZ 2-1 on 11 Nov but went 0-3 at PGL Masters Bucharest recently per tips.gg, and the article calls their group draw unfavorable. Outright odds on Melbet: Spirit 5.00, G2 34.00.
checks.h2h: Last meeting: Spirit beat G2 2-0 in the BLAST Open Porto 2026 upper-bracket semifinal (Fragster, Aug 2026). A scores24 preview for that Porto match noted that in three of the last four meetings Spirit closed out G2 without needing a third map. Earlier 2024-25 meetings were mixed per profilerr, with G2 taking some, so the series is not one-sided.
checks.odds: Polymarket match winner Spirit 0.735 / G2 0.265, flat over the last 24h (price history 0.735 throughout, no move). Polymarket map markets: Map 1 Spirit 0.645, Map 2 Spirit 0.715, Spirit -1.5 maps 0.445, over 2.5 maps 0.415. Melbet outright odds on tips.gg (9 Nov) show a big gap, Spirit 5.00 to win and 2.75 to reach the final versus G2 34.00 and 19.00. I found no direct bookmaker price for this match (no HLTV odds page), so there is no de-vigged second price.
checks.models: No HLTV ranking page was readable. tips.gg says Spirit were in HLTV's top five in mid-October and top two in late October, and that invites were based on VRS Global (Oct 2026). G2 are well below Spirit on both outright odds and form per the same article. No Elo-style model figure found.
checks.venue_weather: LAN at AsiaWorld-Expo, Hong Kong (BLAST Rivals Fall 2026, 11-15 Nov), a standard tier-1 event venue. Group stage is all Bo3. This is not a Bo1, not neutral-unusual, and indoors, so weather is irrelevant.

games.reason: Verified tier-1 BLAST Rivals Fall 2026 Group B Bo3 on LAN (esportnow.gg schedule, Polymarket title confirms Bo3), so not a Bo1 and eligible for the slip. Spirit are the stronger side by ranking, recent title, and a 2-0 win in Aug 2026, which supports the 0.735 market. I keep p at 0.73 because CS2 Bo3 variance is high and Spirit needed three maps yesterday. Rated medium rather than high because no HLTV match page, official lineup confirmation or second bookmaker price was available.
games.main_risk: CS2 Bo3 variance: G2 are a capable upset team (they have beaten Spirit before, mixed 2024-25 results) and just beat MOUZ 2-1. Spirit dropped a map to FUT yesterday, so fatigue or a map-pool veto loss on G2's best maps could cost a map or the series. The winners' match gives G2 a safety net, so Spirit may not be at full intensity, and lineups were not officially confirmed.

games.reason: Hard rule: neutral/unusual venue. This is an NHL Global Series regular-season game played at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki, Finland, not in Carolina (Thu 12 Nov 2026, 12:00 PM ET = 17:00 UTC, 7:00 PM Helsinki local; Kraken are the nominal home team). Hurricanes and Kraken play two games in Helsinki (Nov 12 and Nov 14). Fixture and date verified via Live Nation Finland, TickPick and the Hurricanes site listing; a single SportBusy page listing Seattle's Climate Pledge Arena conflicts with all other sources and is treated as an error. The Polymarket 'home' label (Hurricanes) therefore carries no home-ice edge.
games.main_risk: Neutral European venue with travel/jet lag and no true home advantage; market home price 0.715 is for a nominal 'home' team not playing at home.

checks.team_news: Real Madrid (coach Pedro Martinez) without Facundo Campazzo (left hamstring, out indefinitely, Eurohoops/Sportando 3 Nov), Theo Maledon and Mikael Jantunen (hurt vs Fenerbahce), long-term Gaby Deck and Usman Garuba; Max-Sport/Infobae 11 Nov also list Chuma Okeke as absent while Infobae says Okeke is back in the squad (sources conflict); Nick Smith Jr. cleared from a foot injury; debutant Pablo Mera in the squad. Zvezda (coach Ibon Navarro) travelled to Madrid without centre Christian Koloko because of visa problems, expected to be resolved by Thursday morning (Eurohoops 11 Nov 18:15); no other Zvezda injuries found. The euroleaguebasketball.net injury report returned HTTP 429 and was not used.
checks.lineups: No predicted or confirmed starting fives found in 2 searches (Infobae preview, Eurohoops, Max-Sport 403). Madrid has no Campazzo or Maledon at guard; Koloko's availability for Zvezda is unresolved.
checks.rotation: Madrid: lost Round 10 at home to Panathinaikos 115-112 in OT on Wed 4 Nov, then beat UCAM Murcia 90-71 on Sun 8 Nov (Liga Endesa); about 3-4 days rest, no back-to-back. Next games at Olimpia Milan then Barcelona. Zvezda: won 62-57 at Olympiacos on Fri 6 Nov, 5 days rest, travelling to Madrid. This is a single game week for both, so there is no double-round fatigue.
checks.motivation: Regular season Round 11. Zvezda are 2nd at 7-3; Madrid are 8th at 6-4 after a 6-game winning streak ended vs Panathinaikos. Both need wins for top-4 home court; no rotation or tanking motive.
checks.form: Madrid: 6-game EuroLeague win streak, then OT home loss to Panathinaikos; best offence in the league at 97.8 ppg, depleted backcourt. Zvezda: 7-3, best defence in the league at about 74 ppg allowed, won 103-73 vs Bayern (29 Oct) and 62-57 at Olympiacos (6 Nov).
checks.h2h: 2025-26: Zvezda won 90-75 in Belgrade (17 Oct 2025); Madrid won 95-72 in Madrid; Madrid won 103-82 at Movistar Arena on 16 Apr 2026. Style clash: Madrid's top offence against Zvezda's top defence.
checks.odds: Codere preview: Real Madrid 1.37 / Zvezda 3.05, handicap Madrid -6.5 at 1.85, total 173.5; de-vigged Madrid about 0.69, which matches Polymarket 0.695. No Polymarket 24h move was fetched, so none is claimed. No Stake or Rainbet price seen.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating (net rating, power ranking) was read; only the season scoring and defence averages above. Treated as missing.
checks.venue_weather: Movistar Arena, Madrid (Madrid's home arena, normal venue), Thu 12 Nov 2026, tip-off 20:45-21:00 CET (about 20:00 UTC as listed). Indoor, no weather issue.

games.reason: Fixture verified (EuroLeague Round 11, Real Madrid v Crvena Zvezda, Movistar Arena, Thu 12 Nov). The market 0.695 is already reflected by Codere's de-vigged 0.69. I cut Madrid slightly to 0.67 because Campazzo, Maledon, Jantunen, Deck and Garuba are all out and Madrid lost its last EuroLeague home game depleted. Zvezda have the league's best defence. Madrid's home edge and best offence keep them favoured, and the missing Koloko would help them, but his status is unresolved.
games.main_risk: Depleted Madrid backcourt (no Campazzo or Maledon) against Zvezda's top-ranked defence; a Zvezda upset like the 90-75 win in Oct 2025. Also no lineups, no model rating, and no independent price movement data, so confidence stays low.

checks.team_news: New today: no withdrawal or walkover found for Kostyuk or Gauff. The WTA Day 5 preview (Thursday) still lists Kostyuk, so she is playing as the alternate for Rybakina. It says she had a right wrist injury through the Asian swing, was short of practice, has lost six straight matches (a walkover win over Townsend not counted) and has 15 double faults. It mentions no injury for Gauff, only her serve (broken five times by Noskova, 75% of second-serve points lost). No news was found that explains the price move. Kostyuk's court appearance is not yet confirmed.
checks.lineups: Singles, so no lineup. Order of play now confirmed by the WTA Day 5 preview: [9] Kostyuk v [4] Gauff is first on, 12 p.m. PT (20:00 UTC), then [5] Pegula v [8] Noskova. The Pegula v Noskova result is therefore NOT known before Gauff plays, so it cannot explain the price move. Gauff's path is unchanged: she must beat Kostyuk and Noskova must beat Pegula. An alternate replacing Kostyuk is not indicated.
checks.rotation: Unchanged from the morning. Both players had two days off since Tuesday, so rest is even and travel is nil. Day 1: Gauff d. Pegula 6-4 6-7(5) 6-2, Noskova d. Kostyuk 6-2 6-4. Day 3: Pegula d. Kostyuk 6-2 7-5, Noskova d. Gauff 6-3 6-3. Noskova is through, Kostyuk is out, and Gauff is 1-1.
checks.motivation: Unchanged and confirmed by the WTA preview. Kostyuk is out of contention and playing for pride. Gauff needs the win plus a Noskova win over Pegula, which is decided after her match. She said the goal is just to win the next match. Soft risk: Gauff's motivation edge is smaller than it looks, and she plays without knowing whether she can advance.
